properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 29 at 3:06PM MDT until October 29 at 4:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 306 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain over the Salt Burn Scar. Up to 2 inches of rain have fallen. The
expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour. Additional
rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the Salt burn scar will impact Fence Canyon,
Snow Canyon, Bear Canyon and Turkey Spring Canyon as well as Highway
70 and the Rio Ruidoso through Ruidoso Downs. Impacts may also occur
downstream of Ruidoso Downs along the Rio Ruidoso. The debris flow
can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Salt Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Salt Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ruidoso, Ruidoso Downs, Glencoe and Hollywood.

Increased flow along the Rio Ruidoso from Hollywood to Glencoe may
lead to minor river flooding.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the Salt Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 29 at 2:39PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
ESFABQ

* IMPACTS...River, creek, washes and arroyos may reach out of
banks. Rock, mud and debris may flow into roadways and flash
flooding can not be ruled out, especially in urban areas.

* CONFIDENCE...High confidence in widespread rainfall, with low
confidence in river and flash flooding.

* WHAT...A strong Pacific storm system will interact with a
atmospheric river streaming into the Desert Southwest and Four
Corners region, producing widespread rain which will focus in
the mountains.

* WHERE...Four Corners and surrounding region, including Aztec,
Bloomfield, Farmington and Shiprock.

* WHEN...Sunday into Monday.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...River basins are already saturated from
last week's rainfall and flooding, making additional runoff more
efficient and can more easily cause flooding problems. The
greatest precipitation amounts are forecast in the San Juan
Mountains of Colorado, which will create high flows in the
Animas and La Plata Rivers. These rivers feed the San Juan
River, which saw record flooding last week.

Continue to monitor forecasts for the updates as this situation
unfolds.

Follow NWS Albuquerque on Facebook at: www.facebook.com/NWSAlbuquerque
and on X at: www.x.com/NWSAlbuquerque

properties.areaDesc: Guadalupe Mountains Above 7000 Feet
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 29 at 1:50PM MDT until October 30 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Texas, including the following area,
Guadalupe Mountains Above 7000 Feet.

* WHEN...Through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep moisture will spread over the entire area ahead of an
approaching upper level storm system today and Friday. Numerous
to widespread showers and thunderstorms will be capable of
producing very heavy rainfall over these areas. 1 to 3 inches of
rainfall with locally higher totals will be possible, which could
result in areas of flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Columbia River Bar
properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 29 at 12:29PM PDT until October 29 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Rough bar conditions expected during a very strong ebb
current Thursday evening. Seas peaking near 8 ft and south winds
10 to 15 kt.

* WHERE...In the Main Channel of the Columbia River Bar.

* WHEN...From 5 PM this afternoon to 10 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft,
especially when operating near to, or attempting to cross, the
Columbia River Bar.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Very strong ebb current of 6.5 kt at 732 PM
Thursday. Seas 8 ft.
properties.instruction:
A Small Craft Advisory means that wave conditions are expected to
be hazardous to small craft in the vicinity of the Columbia River
Bar. Mariners are advised to obtain the latest bar conditions
from the United States Coast Guard before attempting to cross the
bar.

properties.areaDesc: Guam Coastal Waters; Rota Coastal Waters; Tinian Coastal Waters; Saipan Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 30 at 5:20AM ChST until October 31 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Seas 7 to 10 feet for Guam and Rota and 11 to 14 feet
for Tinian and Saipan expected.

* WHERE...Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Through 4 PM ChST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...As Super Typhoon In-fa continues to
approach the northern CNMI, seas are quickly building to around
10 feet over Guam and Rota waters and 11 to 14 feet over Tinian
and Siapan waters. The large, long-period swell will slowly
shift from northeast to northwest through Saturday.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid boating in hazardous conditions.

properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 29 at 3:17PM EDT until October 30 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds near 20 kt with gusts up to 25 kt,
especially tonight into Friday morning.

* WHERE...Offshore Gulf waters from the Walton-Okaloosa County
line to the Ochlockonee River from 20 to 60 nautical miles out.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM EDT /1 PM CDT/ Friday.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20
to 33 knots, or seas of 7 feet or greater, are expected to
produce hazardous conditions for small craft. These hazardous
conditions may result in poor vessel handling and steering
response, broaching, overturned dinghies and kayaks, slips and
falls on slippery decks, rub damage along docks and seawalls,
and dragging anchors.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a medium to high chance of winds
exceeding 20 kt tonight over the offshore waters.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.
